solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Going after female is yours truly romancer being over-free?

indicators.note: the words that follow come after the female letter, so it leads the build

parts.note: turned into a question, 'is yours truly' becomes 'am I', with yours truly meaning the speaker
a romancer tells fanciful tales, so is a fibber or teller of untruths

explanation.surface: A man chasing a woman wonders whether his romantic patter makes him a liar and far too forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle reads as a question: 'Am I liar?' coming after F.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too familiar means taking liberties, behaving with excessive freedom towards someone.

clue.text: Shy person in taxi stifling exclamation of discomfort

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the cry sits inside the passenger word

parts.note: a fare is a paying passenger in a cab
ouch is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A timid passenger in a cab suppresses a cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Farouche, borrowed from French, describes someone sullenly timid or unsociable.

clue.text: Saw married man in Germany?

parts.note: Otto is a typical German male name

explanation.surface: Spotting a husband in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but it is the noun for a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same as a guiding phrase.

clue.text: Type of current produces change with fish heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to edit is to change
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A shift in the current brings fish swimming northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: EDIT EEL read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee tide flows with the wind, so it is a kind of tidal current.

clue.text: Pain one gets in hospital? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: gets in signals one piece going inside another
this reverses the stated containment: the hospital letter goes inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient admitted to hospital with a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, ACE would go in H; 'Quite the opposite' puts H inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Inadequate reason for copper to penetrate group in party

indicators.note: the copper symbol goes inside the shortened word, piercing it
inadequate means falling short, so the synonym for reason loses its final letter

parts.note: a reason for something is its cause
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A weak excuse for a policeman to infiltrate a political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inadequate' trims CAUSE to CAUS; 'copper' is the chemical element, not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a meeting or bloc of members within a political party.

clue.text: Dye — an international organisation consumes tons

indicators.note: consumes means swallows, so the tons letter goes inside

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation

explanation.surface: An international body gets through tons of colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatto is an orange-red food colouring made from achiote seeds.

clue.text: Visitor getting round to entertain a British gentleman abroad

indicators.note: to entertain means to take in as a guest, so the inner pieces go inside

parts.note: a caller is someone who visits
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A visitor makes the rounds hosting a British gentleman overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: CALLER + O takes A + B inside, after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is the Spanish word for a gentleman or knight, hence one met abroad.

clue.text: After sun wait — till the sky becomes this?

indicators.note: after means the waiting word follows the sun letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun, as in Sunday
to tarry is to linger or wait

explanation.surface: After sunset, waiting until the sky looks a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cryptic tail: wait after sunset until the night sky shows its lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A night sky full of visible stars is described as star-filled, which is what the clue's waiting achieves.

clue.text: Somewhere in Yorkshire the woman's tucking into rubbish meat

indicators.note: tucking into means placing the pronoun inside, here between the two outer words

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
ham is a cured meat
her is the possessive for 'the woman'

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire woman eating a plate of poor-quality meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, but it means HER goes inside ROTHAM. Rotherham is a town in South Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Rotherham lies in South Yorkshire, England, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: Something flowery — dress past its best mum's put on

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed on top, so it comes first

parts.note: ma is mum, the mother
rig is clothing or outfit
old means worn and past its prime

explanation.surface: A floral frock that is past its best has been worn by mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' suggests wearing the dress, but in a down clue it means mother's word sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a yellow or orange garden flower.

clue.text: Excellent bit of food seen around old part of Africa

indicators.note: seen around means the letters are viewed turned round, read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
a bun is a small item of food

explanation.surface: A fine snack is spotted somewhere on an ancient African tour.
explanation.walkthrough: AI BUN read backwards gives the answer; A1, the shipping-register mark for top quality, is written AI here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia was an ancient region along the Nile, in present-day Sudan and southern Egypt.

clue.text: Heaven on earth without opiates denied some

indicators.note: the words are denied some of their letters at each end, leaving a run inside them

explanation.surface: Paradise is a world free of drugs, though some people are deprived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like part of the definition or a deletion signal, but it is just where the letters begin: withOUT OPIAtes.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopia is an imagined perfect society, a paradise on earth.

clue.text: One feels one must talk quietly with snake behind

indicators.note: the snake comes behind the quiet letter, following it
the snake comes behind the quiet letter, following it

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
a rattler is a rattlesnake

explanation.surface: Someone feels compelled to speak softly with a serpent at their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... behind' places RATTLER after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterer is someone who feels compelled to keep talking idly and endlessly.

clue.text: One making attempt to pursue success is less cheerful

indicators.note: to pursue means to follow, so this comes after the success

parts.note: a win is a success
a trier is someone who tries

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps chasing success ends up gloomier.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry can mean cold and unfriendly in manner, so the comparative means colder in mood.

clue.text: Emphasising to good effect, banging on the wall maybe

definitions.meaning: driving a point forcefully so it is understood
literally, using a mallet on something in the house, such as knocking a nail into a wall

explanation.surface: Someone making a point forcefully while thumping the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: striking with a mallet in one's own house.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer a point home is an idiom for stressing it until it lands; literally it is pounding at home.

clue.text: Martha's sister hides a sign of something wrong, bad in the jaw

indicators.note: hides means conceals, so the pieces go inside the name

parts.note: in the Bible, Martha's sister is Mary of Bethany
a cross is the mark for a wrong answer
ill means bad

explanation.surface: Mary, Martha's sister, conceals a painful problem in her jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Martha and Mary are sisters in the Gospels; X is the cross marking a wrong answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxillary is the adjective for the maxilla, the upper jawbone, so it means relating to the jaw.

clue.text: Painter mixing reds only

indicators.note: mixing means blending together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist mixes nothing but red shades on the palette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' rearranges REDS ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joshua Reynolds was an 18th-century English portrait artist.

clue.text: Replace sex toy, damaged instrument

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap out a broken adult toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges REPLACE SEX TOY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a scientific device for observing high-energy radiation from space, a type of instrument.

clue.text: Article received by a servant as a royal perk?

indicators.note: received by means taken in, so the article goes inside

parts.note: a page is a young servant
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item handed to a servant as a perk from the royals.
explanation.definitionFit: An apanage was land or income granted to younger royal children, a privilege of rank.

clue.text: Queen to have extra time looking around, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is said aloud and the sound is spelt differently

parts.words: to have extra time looking around
parts.note: being able to look around for longer is to get to see more

explanation.surface: A monarch wants longer to look around the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see more' said aloud is the surname of Henry VIII's third wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Seymour was Henry VIII's third wife and so an English queen consort.

clue.text: Before beginning to move I remain in the same place

indicators.note: before means these come ahead of the final letter

parts.note: to bide is to stay or remain

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone stays put before starting to move.
explanation.walkthrough: I + BIDE before M.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin meaning 'in the same source', used in references for a citation already given.

clue.text: Country song swelling briefly at the start

indicators.note: the shortened swelling comes at the start, ahead of the song
briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a bulge is a swelling
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A country song that briefly builds up at its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts BULGE to BULG.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a nation in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Protein this person's bone has inside

parts.note: the speaker's own, i.e. my
os is Latin for bone, used in anatomy
in means inside

explanation.surface: A claim that the speaker's bones contain a certain protein.
explanation.walkthrough: MY + OS + IN; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Myosin is a protein found in muscle fibres, working with actin in contraction.

clue.text: Odd bits of song about country girl

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters wrap the country
odd bits means the first and third letters of the word

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Fragments of a country-and-western song about a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' sits by 'girl' as though 'country girl', but it is a separate piece; 'Odd bits of' takes the first and third letters of 'song'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Susan is a common female given name, so it stands for any girl.

clue.text: Provided with men, MD sacked woman

indicators.note: sacked means dismissed, so those letters are removed

parts.note: staffed with people, crewed
the managing director's initials, the letters M and D

explanation.surface: Given a male workforce, the managing director fired a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MD' reads as a doctor or boss, but its two letters are what 'sacked' removes, one from each end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Anne is a familiar female given name, standing for a woman in general.

clue.text: Histrionics when tot confronts adult

indicators.note: confronts means stands facing, so the measure comes before the adult letter

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A tantrum erupts when a toddler squares up to a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child but is a measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a drama of something means overreacting theatrically, which is histrionic behaviour.

clue.text: It's no use, girl being abused as 'bird'

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl objects that it is pointless to be insulted as a 'bird'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like British slang for a young woman, but it is the definition. 'being abused' rearranges NO USE GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring ouzel is a thrush of upland Europe with a white breast band.

clue.text: Early life with drug (not soft)? That spells trouble

parts.note: May, spring, figuratively the prime or youth of life

indicators.note: not means without, so the soft letter is removed

parts.note: hemp is cannabis
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Youthful days spent on a drug that isn't a mild one spell trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY for the springtime of life, plus HEMP losing P.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is chaos and disorder, a state of serious trouble.

clue.text: After fiddling, earns big position

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After some dodgy accounting, a person earns a big job.
explanation.definitionFit: One's bearings are one's sense of location or orientation, one's place relative to surroundings.
